For we too say that the baptism you have comes from the Lord's body, that is, from the church, even though you yourselves are not in it, like all who build not on the rock but on sand. Why, then, do you not notice that the water by which you say baptism was signified was not only in the Lord's body but also came out of his body, and did so through a wound inflicted by a persecutor? Heretics and all the wicked would not have taken the sacraments outside with them if they had kept the wholeness of unity in the Lord's body. But you see how deep even this is, and how profound the mystery in which it is hidden.

That is enough. Stop arguing in this way. Everything of this kind that you put forward is either for us or, to understate our case greatly, it is uncertain whom it favours. But you gladly linger over what is hidden so that you will not be forced to admit what is plain. Here is the church! What is wrong with you, I ask? Here is the church, commended and portrayed, foretold and shown by so many very clear testimonies of the holy scriptures: "As we have heard, so we have seen." Why do you evade the question of how you are to be received? Why do you refuse to be received in the way she receives, she to whom he who could not lie bears witness? Show that the canonical scriptures have stated plainly that someone baptized among heretics in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit must be baptized in the Catholic Church. If you cannot show that, then show that some plain and clear testimony is given by the canonical scriptures to your communion, the party of Donatus, where you learned this. Then I will admit that I must cross over to you, and that heretics should be received only as the church you belong to receives them, since she has been declared by such testimony. Why are you agitated? Why are you troubled? You cannot find in the canonical scriptures what we quite rightly demand of you. As for what you usually cite, "Where do you pasture, where do you lie down at noon?", you see what sort of text it is and how little it favours you. So do not go looking for texts like that. If the party of Donatus were in the northern regions, which are opposite the southern regions, it would say that this was said of itself: "Mount Zion, the sides of the north, the city of the great king." Surely the city of the great king is nothing other than the church, and this text points to the church more unmistakably than "Where do you pasture, where do you lie down at noon?" But perhaps Marcion the heretic would use that text, since he is said to have been from Pontus, which lies to the north. Again, if the party of Donatus were in the west, it would say that this was said of itself: "Make a way for him who rises above the setting sun; the Lord is his name." Perhaps it would say that "he rises above the setting sun" is loftier than "he lies down at noon." These texts are mystical, hidden, figurative. We demand of you something plain that needs no interpreter.

So I receive you as the seed of Abraham receives you, in which all nations are blessed. This would perhaps be obscure if Paul had not revealed that the seed of Abraham is Christ. I receive you as the barren woman receives you, whose children are more than those of the woman who has a husband. This would be obscure if Paul had not said that she is the church, our mother. To her it was said: "The Lord who delivered you shall himself be called the God of the whole earth"; to her it was said: "Your land shall be the whole world." I receive you as that queen receives you, of whom it is said in the psalms, "The queen stood at your right hand," and to whom it is said, "In place of your fathers, sons have been born to you; you will make them princes over all the earth." Finally, not to list many more, I receive you as the church receives you, the church throughout all nations, beginning from Jerusalem, the church which is Christ's witness in Jerusalem and in all Judea and Samaria and to the whole earth. For it is he who receives you who said this of her, who pointed her out in such words so that no one should doubt about her. I receive you as the wheat sown in the field receives you, which grows with the weeds until the harvest. For these are the children of the kingdom, the field is the world, and the harvest is the end of the age. The Lord explained it; it is the gospel; these are the Lord's words, and they are plain. I could say to you: "I receive you the way you received those whom Praetextatus and Felicianus baptized outside your communion when you had condemned them," and to that you have no answer at all. But I will rather say something that holds unanswerably even against the Maximianists themselves, who have thoroughly defeated you on the two texts you use most often and yet most ignorantly: the one about fewness and the one about noon. So I will say this, which silences all of you, as if you were rising against us together: "We receive you, if you are willing to be corrected, as the church receives you. The Lord Jesus said she would begin from Jerusalem, and we read in the Acts of the Apostles that she began there. He said she would go through all nations, and we read in the Acts of the Apostles that she went through many of them before she came to Africa. And she will go through all of them before the end comes, for the Lord himself says: 'This gospel will be preached among all nations, and then the end will come.'" Here is her chaff: "Because iniquity will abound, the love of many will grow cold." Here is her wheat: "But whoever perseveres to the end will be saved." Where in this is Africa named in the party of Donatus? Here again is her wheat: "So that you may know," says the apostle, "how you ought to conduct yourself in the house of God, which is the church of the living God, the pillar and foundation of the truth. And without doubt great is the mystery of godliness, which was manifested in the flesh, justified in the Spirit, appeared to angels, was preached among the nations, believed in the world, taken up in glory." Here is her chaff: "Now the Spirit says plainly," he says, "that in the last times some will depart from the faith, giving heed to seducing spirits and doctrines of demons," and the rest. Where here too is Africa named in the party of Donatus, as though the pillar and foundation of the truth, or the mystery of godliness, had remained in it? Of that mystery he ran on to the end, saying: "preached among the nations, believed in the world, taken up in glory."

Why should I hold you any longer? Whoever thinks of replying to this letter, let him search the scriptures and produce a clear testimony about Africa, in which alone, or from which alone, the party of Donatus exists. He cannot produce one, because scripture cannot contradict the very clear testimonies we have produced. Or else, if he is seeking credulous followers for his suspicions, accusations and slanders, and wants to lead them over to another gospel, which is no other gospel, and to proclaim to us something beyond what we have received, then even if he were an angel from heaven he would be anathema. For the devil fell from heaven because he did not stand in the truth. When he proclaimed to man something beyond what man had received from the Lord God, if he had been anathema to him, the first parents of our flesh would neither have incurred the penalty of death nor left the place of happiness.

Therefore, dearly beloved, to whom I write this letter, hold fast with most faithful and steadfast hearts to the command of the shepherd who laid down his life for his sheep and now, glorified and exalted, sits at the right hand of God the Father. He says: "My sheep hear my voice and follow me." You have heard his voice very plainly, not only through his law and the prophets and the psalms, but also from his own mouth, as he commended his church that was to come. And when you read the Acts and the letters of the apostles, which complete the canon of the divine scriptures, you see clearly how what he foretold followed in due order. This is not an obscure question in which you can be deceived by those whom the Lord himself foretold would come and say: "Look, here is the Christ! Look, there he is! Look, he is in the desert," as though he were where there is no great multitude; "Look, he is in the inner rooms," as though in secret traditions and teachings. You have it that the church is spread everywhere and grows until the harvest. You have the city of which he who founded it says: "A city set on a hill cannot be hidden." She, then, is the church, known far and wide, not in one part of the world only but everywhere. Sometimes she suffers storms for a time, even among her own wheat, so that in some places she is not recognized; yet even there she is present though hidden. The divine word cannot be mistaken, since both grow until the harvest.

So it has often happened among other nations, too, that some members of the church were oppressed and overshadowed when the turmoil of heresies and schisms prevailed. Yet because they were there, shortly afterwards they shone out beyond anyone's doubt. In Africa itself the same happened after the seditious and turbulent council of Secundus of Tigisis at Carthage, where the corruption worked by the noblewoman Lucilla was later recorded in judicial proceedings. Letters were sent from that council through almost the whole of Africa, wherever the churches of Christ had already sprung up, and the letters of the council were believed, since it was not right to do otherwise. It seemed as though the Lord's wheat had failed in some part of the field. But it had by no means failed, for it was truly wheat, predestined and sown, deeply rooted and growing fruitfully. Those people had believed the council's letters with a clear conscience. Nothing incredible was being said by some men about other men, and nothing was believed that went against the gospel. But afterwards those men, with frenzied obstinacy, carried their most stubborn quarrel to the point of a sacrilegious schism against the whole Christian world. Then the good believers whom false accusation had turned against Caecilian came to realize that if they remained in that communion, they would be passing a perverse judgment, no longer about some man or some men, but about the church spread throughout the whole world. They chose to believe the gospel of Christ rather than the council of their colleagues. So many bishops, clergy and lay people soon left them and returned to Catholic peace. Even before they did so they were counted among the wheat, for they were not yet doing this while their opposition was directed against men falsely represented to them by their colleagues, and not against the church of God, which grows among all nations. So in Africa, too, the wheat that the Son of Man had sown remained wheat. From that time until now it has grown and is growing, and from now until the harvest it will bear fruit and grow, as it does throughout the whole world.

Some people of good will, however, through the darkness of the flesh, remained in error in that schism for quite a long time, even after the fury of the wicked against the church of God had become entrenched. It was as if the wheat were being trampled while still tender and the vigour of the green blade crushed while its root was alive. Yet God knew these too as his wheat, though they had to be rebuked and reproved so that they might come to life again. For "Get behind me, Satan" was not said to Peter in the same sense in which it was said of Judas, "One of you is a devil." Some also opposed the plainest truth with ill will. These were uprooted or cut off. But they did not persist in unbelief, as the apostle says of certain broken branches, and so they were replanted or grafted in again by the hand of God. A person is unfruitful but not yet cut off from the root when, out of evil desire, he does the works of which it is said: "Those who do such things will not possess the kingdom of God." But when, for the sake of those works, he also begins to resist the plainest truth by which he is refuted, then he is cut off. And there are many such people who share the sacraments with the church and yet are no longer in the church. Otherwise, if a person is cut off only when he is visibly excommunicated, it will follow that he is grafted in again when he is visibly restored to communion. What, then, if someone approaches insincerely, bearing a heart utterly hostile to the truth and to the church? Even if that ceremony is performed over him, is he reconciled? Is he grafted in? Certainly not. Just as such a man, though now in communion again, has not yet been grafted in, so anyone who bears a hostile mind against the truth by which he is convicted and refuted is already cut off, even before he is visibly excommunicated. So it comes about that both the good seed and the bad seed grow throughout the field until the harvest, that is, both the children of the kingdom and the children of the evil one grow throughout the world until the end of the age. The former bear fruit with patience; the latter grow bitter in their barrenness.

But you, relying on so many very clear testimonies of the law, the prophets and the psalms, and of the Lord himself and the apostles, about the holy church spread throughout the whole world, demand that these people show some clear testimonies from the canonical books about Africa, as it concerns the party of Donatus. For, as I have already said, it could not possibly be that the church, which according to them (God forbid!) was to perish so quickly from so many nations, should be proclaimed by so many testimonies, so loftily and so unmistakably, while scripture kept silent about the church they want to claim as their own, which on their account was to last until the end. Remember what was said to that rich man when he was in torment in the underworld and wanted someone from the dead to be sent to his brothers: "They have Moses and the prophets there," he was told. And when he said that they would not believe unless someone from the dead went to them, the answer was: "If they do not listen to Moses and the prophets, neither will they believe if someone rises from the dead." Moses said that in the seed of Abraham all nations would be blessed. The prophets said: "You shall be called My Delight, and your land the whole world," and: "All the ends of the earth will remember and turn to the Lord." These people refused to believe these prophecies and others like them, which point to the church so plainly. The Lord rose from the dead and said that repentance and the forgiveness of sins should be preached in his name among all nations, beginning from Jerusalem. Those who had not believed Moses and the prophets did not believe the Lord when he rose from the dead either. What remains for them but to share the torments of that rich man? Flee those torments while there is still time, before you depart this life. Hold firmly to the divine words, so that you will not be thrown into confusion in this life, and after this life you will be found worthy to receive what was promised to the seed of Abraham.
